B. Cycle by cycle: three sends, the third behind a two-packet return
t: a is captured; t+1: a goes out while b is captured (no stall: the register is being emptied). t+2, t+3: a 128-bit return holds the
injection point for two packets, so b waits and the store of c stalls. t+4: b goes out and c is captured; t+5: c goes out.
hold the ROUTER_SEND_LO store this cycle
the packet was injected this cycle
• No checks at the sender (§4.11): an invalid mode, mode 1 to another tile, or dst 65 (unused) go out as written; the receiver drops a bad mode (condition 9 there), and the simulator checks the rest.
ROUTER_SET_HDR and ROUTER_SET_HI are undefined at chip reset (§8).
A ROUTER_SEND_LO store captures the header, the high word and its own data into the one-packet holding register; the header's addr then
steps by the words the packet writes, and ROUTER_SET_HI clears. The store stalls only while the register is full and not leaving this cycle,
so sends run one a cycle unless read returns, which go first, hold the injection point.
